messages.subject: HPDI and credible interval
parts:
Hi blavaan users!
Sorry for this basic question:
May I write that the 95%HPDI (Highest posterior density interval) is the 95% credible interval?
Do you know references where I can get an answer?
Best,
csm

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: HPDI and credible interval
parts: May I write that the 95%HPDI (Highest posterior density interval) is the 95% credible interval?

Yes, CI is an umbrella term for many types of interval estimates.  An HPD CI is a special case that contains the 95% most likely values.  The one you are probably familiar with is the normal-theory CI (the point estimate +/- some number of SEs). 

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

messages.author: 645e2b041ea2a63e
messages.subject: Re: HPDI and credible interval
parts:
In addition to what Terrence wrote, I would add the "percentile-based"
Bayesian credible interval, where, e.g., for a 90% interval you find
the 5th percentile and 95th percentile of all the sampled parameter
values (where the samples are drawn via MCMC).

This will be similar to the HPD interval when the posterior
distribution is symmetric (which is often the case). But the HPD
interval becomes preferable when the posterior is skewed.

Ed
